entries.name: FEDEX_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The API key of a FedEx Developer Portal project with the Track API. FedEx calls it the client id; it is sent to FedEx only, with the secret, to sign in.
howToGet: Sign in at developer.fedex.com with the business's FedEx account and create a project for KaratOS.
Choose only the Track API, link the shipping account, and copy the production API key.

entries.name: FEDEX_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The project's secret key. With only the Track API chosen, it can read tracking and nothing else: no labels, pickups or billing.
howToGet: On the same project's page at developer.fedex.com, copy the production secret key.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: FEDEX_TRACKING_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the FedEx tracking numbers to follow, one or more a line, such as the labels printed for repairs, memo goods and customer orders. Lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the tracking numbers from FedEx Ship Manager's history, the POS or the shipping app.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers as parcels go out; delivered ones are no longer read.

entries.name: FEDEX_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production (the default) reads live tracking; test uses FedEx's sandbox, which only answers its own test numbers.

entries.name: FEDEX_MAX_TRACKING_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most tracking numbers one sync reads, oldest first. Defaults to 500, so a long list stays well inside FedEx's daily call limit.
